+def _is_mul_or_quotient(expr):
+    """Check if ``expr`` is printed as a product or as a quotient.
+
+    This is the case for expressions like ``2*x``, ``1/2``, ``1/x`` or
+    ``1/sqrt(x)``.  Such an expression cannot be used as a factor of the
+    denominator of a division without being parenthesized, e.g. ``x/(1/y)``
+    and not ``x/1/y`` (the latter would be parsed back as ``x/y``).
+
+    """
+    if isinstance(expr, Mul):
+        return True
+    if isinstance(expr, Rational):
+        # a rational number is printed as a quotient, e.g. 1/2, unless
+        # it is an integer
+        return expr.q != 1
+    if isinstance(expr, Pow):
+        # a commutative Pow with exponent -1 or -1/2 is printed as
+        # 1/x respectively 1/sqrt(x)
+        return (expr.is_commutative and
+                (expr.exp == S.NegativeOne or expr.exp == -S.Half))
+    return False
+
+
 class StrPrinter(Printer):
     printmethod = "_sympystr"
     _default_settings = {
